thread:
eve_customer: Hi team — since the 1.8.2 runtime deploy our requests to model endpoints in eu-west-1 are intermittently routed to us-east-1, adding ~180ms. Billing is getting counted to us-east too. Noticed around 2025-06-12 10:05 UTC. Can someone look?

alice_support: Thanks for the report, @eve_customer. Sorry about the hit — can you paste a curl (with headers) that reproduces the wrong-region routing? Also sending ticket #SUP-4821.

eve_customer: Sure — reproducer:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response shows header: \"x-served-region: us-east-1\" and latency ~210ms.

alice_support: Copying in infra/eng: @ben_infra @dmitri_engineering — appears to be L7 routing selecting wrong cluster despite explicit X-Redwood-Region.

dmitri_engineering: Looking. Do we have logs for that request id? If you can share the response headers (x-request-id, x-served-region) I'll trace it in Envoy access logs.

eve_customer: x-request-id: req_62c9... , x-served-region: us-east-1, timestamp: 2025-06-12T10:06:14Z.

ben_infra: I pulled the access log for req_62c9... — Envoy hit route matcher in L7 vhost for api.redwood.ai and chose cluster "us-east-1-prod". The route config should prefer the X-Redwood-Region rewrite and route to eu-west-1 cluster. Suspect header precedence changed after Envoy 1.24 bump (we rolled in 1.24.1 two nights ago).

carla_sre: Repro on our side: I sent same curl from a probe in eu-west-1 and got us-east-1 cluster 3/10 tries. Flags: region header present, but downstream-filter rewrite doesn't seem to persist to route selection on some code paths.

dmitri_engineering: This smells like https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/issues/12345 — header evaluation order for :authority/Host vs custom header when SNI/ALPN negotiation changes listener context. Our route rule checks header matcher first, then host. If the header is being dropped by the HTTP/2 connection pool or by the TLS terminator, fallback to geo routing kicks in.

alice_support: Quick ask: can we mitigate customer impact while root cause is investigated? Options: temporary config to force region routing by host prefix, or add a header rewrite at ingress to copy X-Redwood-Region -> x-envoy-upstream-region (whatever route matcher reads).

ben_infra: I pushed a canary Envoy route override on prod-internal to rewrite and set a synthetic header 'x-route-region' from X-Redwood-Region before route matching. Config snippet: 
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local r = request_handle:headers():get("x-redwood-region")
        if r ~= nil then
          request_handle:headers():add("x-route-region", r)
        end
      end
```
Canary applied to 5% of traffic to verify.

dmitri_engineering: Confirmed trace shows the canary route uses x-route-region to pick eu-west-1 correctly. Need to roll to 100% and then propose a permanent fix in the route matcher.

alice_support: @eve_customer we applied a 5% canary with the header-rewrite; can you retry your reproducer a few times and report if you still see us-east responses?

eve_customer: Retried 10 times at 10:25 UTC — 0/10 wrong region now, latency down to ~28ms. Big improvement. Thanks.

carla_sre: We'll keep canary at 5% for 20 minutes then ramp. Suggest change-list: (1) backport header-rewrite filter to 1.23 branch, (2) adjust route config to match x-route-region explicitly, (3) open Envoy bug report pinned to the upgrade so we don't regress.

dmitri_engineering: I'll open ENG-REQ-1102 for the permanent change and assign to runtime team. Also filing a coordinated rollback plan if 1.24-only behaviour is the cause.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollout: envoy-route-override canary -> prod-internal (5%) started by ben_infra at 2025-06-12T10:18:00Z.

alice_support: Marking SUP-4821 as escalated -> ENG. I'll update customer with progress. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
